title: Asia-Pacific Youth Want Real-World Work Skills
paragraphs: Young people in the Asia-Pacific region feel that school is not fully preparing them for the world of work, and they want more chances to gain real-world experience, according to a new study.

The study, called "Shaping Tomorrow's Workforce: Asia Pacific Youth Insights," was carried out by the delivery company FedEx and Junior Achievement, an organization that teaches young people about work and money. In June and July, the researchers surveyed 4,219 young people aged 15 to 22 in ten markets across the region.

The results showed a clear gap between education and work. Around 90% of respondents said they saw a difference between what they learn at school and the skills they will need in their future jobs. Even more, 97%, said they need opportunities to gain direct, hands-on experience.

Many young people also lack confidence in some important skills. Only 55% said they felt comfortable solving problems that have no obvious right answer, and 59% felt confident about working independently and making decisions with little guidance.

When asked which skills they most want to develop, respondents put workplace experience, problem-solving and creative thinking at the top. These were followed by communication, presentation and digital skills.
Artificial intelligence is another concern. According to FedEx, 84% of respondents expect to work alongside AI in the future, but only 62% believe their education is preparing them to use it at work.

There were also differences between countries. Malaysia was the only market where young people ranked digital skills as their top priority. Young people in Southeast Asia rated their own ability to show initiative and make independent decisions more highly than those in South Korea and Japan.

Youth unemployment in the region is nearly 14%. Executives from FedEx and Junior Achievement said that solving this problem will require more practical, industry-led training to help young people develop the skills that employers are looking for.
